answer: Admission requires a uniquely allocated IPv4 prefix with a published RPKI ROA and a slashable deposit. Jurors send a challenge packet that must be signed from that prefix; a reused prefix, a missing ROA, or a signature that did not originate on the announced route burns the deposit and bars the key. Because IPv4 is scarce, each fake identity costs another purchased prefix, another year of RIR fees, and another full deposit — linear, and worse as leftover blocks vanish. The looking-glass sits under a vine on shale at the foot of a glacier road, yet only the ROA and on-prefix signature count.
